name: Helix Biosystems Olfactory Gradient Probe
description:
The Olfactory Gradient Probe is a handheld chemical plume detection and source-location instrument that uses an array of 2,400 synthetic chemoreceptor filaments to identify, classify, and triangulate the origin point of airborne chemical signatures. Unlike conventional gas detectors that simply alert to the presence of a substance, the OGP maps concentration gradients across space — effectively 'smelling' which direction a scent is getting stronger — and uses that gradient data to compute a vector toward the emission source. The chemoreceptor array is modeled on vertebrate olfactory epithelium but operates at a sensitivity roughly 80 times greater than baseline human olfaction, capable of detecting compounds at parts-per-trillion concentrations.

Helix Biosystems engineered the OGP originally for pharmaceutical contamination tracing in clean-room environments, but the probe's utility in field applications became rapidly apparent. The device can identify over 14,000 indexed chemical signatures including explosives precursors, specific pharmaceutical compounds, biological markers associated with stress responses (adrenaline metabolites, cortisol derivatives present in sweat), and the proprietary chemical tracers used by several major corporations to mark restricted personnel and assets. A rolling update subscription keeps the chemical index current. The probe's interface presents gradient data as a directional compass overlay with confidence percentages, and can log a full chemical environment profile for later forensic analysis.

The OGP occupies an uncomfortable legal space in GLMZ. Its capacity to detect stress-chemistry signatures means it can effectively identify frightened or nervous individuals in a crowd — a capability that law enforcement, corporate interrogators, and bounty hunters find enormously attractive and civil liberties advocates find deeply troubling. Helix markets it carefully as an 'industrial and forensic instrument,' but its presence in less scrupulous hands is an open secret.

specifications.detection_range: Active sampling to 15m; gradient source triangulation to 60m in still air
specifications.biological_markers: Adrenaline metabolites, cortisol derivatives, fear-sweat compound profiles
specifications.interface: Directional compass overlay with confidence percentage, chemical ID readout
specifications.logging: Full chemical environment profile capture for forensic export

tactical_use: Operators use the OGP to sweep rooms for hidden individuals using stress-chemistry signatures before entry, trace the path of a target through a space by following adrenaline-metabolite trails, and detect concealed explosives or contraband by identifying precursor compounds. Bounty hunters use it to locate hiding targets in complex environments. Corporate security teams use it to identify unauthorized personnel carrying proprietary chemical tracers. Forensic investigators use it to reconstruct who was present in a space and their approximate physiological state during an incident.
cultural_context: The OGP has generated significant cultural anxiety in GLMZ's lower districts, where residents fear corporate security teams sweeping public spaces for stress markers — effectively scanning crowds for anyone nervous enough to be flagged as suspicious. 'Running hot' has become street slang for displaying stress chemistry that would register on a Bloodhound scan. Some underground pharmacies sell compounds that temporarily suppress adrenaline metabolite production, marketed euphemistically as 'calm supplements.' The device is both a serious professional instrument and a symbol of invasive surveillance overreach depending entirely on who's holding it.
known_users: Helix Biosystems internal security and R&D compliance teams
Underground counter-surveillance consultants (to understand what clients face)
story_hooks: A character discovers their safe house has been swept by an OGP — whoever did it now has a full chemical profile of everyone who was present, including stress states during specific moments
A street pharmacist is selling 'calm supplements' that actually suppress OGP-detectable markers — corporate security wants to know who's supplying counter-measure drugs to the population
An OGP sweep at a corporate gala identifies a specific attendee as carrying a proprietary tracer belonging to a rival corporation — but the attendee claims never to have worked for that corp
A character needs to move through a corporate facility where OGP sweeps are conducted — they have 18 minutes to find a route before the device's battery logs are transmitted to security central

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, elongated sensor wand resembling a high-tech dowsing rod or diagnostic probe. The form factor is purposefully clinical and precise — narrower grip section tapering toward a slightly bulbous sensing head studded with microscopic receptor filaments. The overall aesthetic straddles professional laboratory instrument and field-deployed tactical tool.
physical_description.dimensions: 280mm length × 45mm grip diameter × 35mm at sensor head. Roughly the size of a large marker or small flashlight.
physical_description.weight_description: 340g; handheld and pocketable with carrying case, no strap required but often worn in hip-mounted holster for field operatives.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite body with embedded conductive traces; sensor head features bioengineered synthetic chemoreceptor array housed in optically transparent biofilm membrane.
physical_description.finish: Matte textured polymer grip with soft-touch coating; sensor head has faint iridescent sheen from membrane, reminiscent of insect exoskeleton. Minimal reflectivity by design.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with deep teal accents around sensor head. Helix Biosystems branding in chrome. Faint bioluminescent accent strip along grip (indicator status).
physical_description.interface_elements: Small high-contrast LCD display (30mm) mounted on grip showing directional compass, confidence percentage, and chemical identifier. Three tactile buttons (scan, index, log). USB-C charging port masked by textured cap. Micro-OLED overlay capable of AR integration with user's visual neural interface.
distinctive_features: Microscopic chemoreceptor filament array visible as fine crystalline matrix across sensor head surface
Soft pulsing bioluminescent status indicator (green=ready, amber=scanning, red=high-concentration alert) running along grip edge
Helix Biosystems embossed logo with registered trademark and 'LEGAL FORENSIC ONLY' disclaimer etched in microtext
Faint organic shimmer to sensor membrane — biological component references its olfactory epithelium origin
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (stylized double helix) in chrome on grip. Model designation OGP-7.2 laser-etched. Serial number and regulatory compliance stamps (GLMZ-EPA-APPROVED, CORPS-LICENSED) on base. Subscription status indicator on display.
physical_description.condition_typical: In field use, the probe is held at arm's length, swept side-to-side like a metal detector. Display continuously updates directional bearing and concentration gradient. Chemoreceptor filaments may show microscopic wear after extensive use; biofilm membrane occasionally requires refresh (proprietary cartridge, Φ240 per replacement). Dust and residue accumulation on sensor head is common; requires careful cleaning with provided solvent swab.
